author: Mark Atwood
text:
Workspace-policy decision required between two coherent paths. The bead body presents (a) and (b) without a recommendation.

Recommendation: path (a) — pub(crate) + tests/common wrapper.

Rationale:

(1) The workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' rule is explicit: when a sibling diverges from the canonical jmap-mail-server, change the canonical first then propagate, OR propagate the sibling to match the canonical. Mail-server has zero *_for_test mutation knobs on its MemoryBackend; chat-server is the divergent sibling. Path (a) realigns the cookie-cutter. Path (b) ratifies the divergence and asks the workspace to update the rule.

(2) Path (b) inverts the canonical-template rule for one specific class of API surface ('MemoryBackend test-seam helpers'). Adopting it as policy would then require justifying which OTHER divergent surfaces also get the 'reference impl is its own thing' carve-out and which stay under cookie-cutter discipline. That is a wider scope than this single bead.

(3) The four chat-server methods correspond to four distinct test-seam needs that all have wrapper-friendly shapes:

    - set_retains_edit_history_for_test / set_protect_last_admin_for_test: boolean policy knobs. Could ALSO be exposed via a pub MemoryBackend::set_policy(ChatPolicy) method that takes a typed struct of policy switches (the same struct shape ChatLimits uses for caps). That would be canonical-template aligned because mail-server doesn't have these policies but the *shape* is wrapper-free.

    - set_limits_for_test: limits override. The canonical pattern per workspace AGENTS.md 'Backend caps and limits' is for production backends to override the limits() trait method, not to mutate a stored cap struct. But integration tests need to vary limits without writing a new backend. A pub MemoryBackend::with_limits(ChatLimits) builder (and matching set_limits without the _for_test suffix) would be canonical-template aligned (the calendars-server analog would land in the same shape during the CalendarsLimits override-via-Inner-field follow-up).

    - insert_object_for_test: seed without bumping state / change log. This is exactly seed_object (which already exists at line 367 of chat-server memory.rs via the same shape). The two are sibling helpers — insert_object_for_test should be renamed seed_object and the existing seed_object reviewed for whether it duplicates the new one. Possibly path (a) collapses these.

Path (a) implementation outline if accepted:

  1. Move all four pub fn into pub(crate) at chat-server/src/memory.rs.
  2. Add a wrapper struct or set of pub fn in chat-server/tests/common/mod.rs that exposes the same operations to integration tests. (Or expose them as pub fn directly on a MemoryTestExt trait that integration tests import.)
  3. Find-and-replace the 63 call sites across 8 test files.
  4. Verify cargo test -p jmap-chat-server passes.
  5. Verify cargo clippy -p jmap-chat-server passes.
  6. cargo doc -p jmap-chat-server with RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings'.

Estimated effort: 2-3 hours of mechanical refactor. No production code paths touched. Bisectable per-file.

Path (a) reasonable variations:

  - (a.1) Bare pub(crate) helpers + tests/common/mod.rs wrapper functions that take &MemoryBackend and forward via crate-private internals. Requires the wrapper to live INSIDE the chat-server crate's tests/ tree to access pub(crate) items. Standard pattern.

  - (a.2) Keep the methods pub on MemoryBackend but require a feature flag (e.g. 'memory-test-helpers') that is not enabled by default. Adds a feature surface that needs documenting. Diverges from canonical mail-server which uses neither pub(crate)+common nor a separate feature.

Recommend (a.1).

Alternative path (b) consideration:

  If path (b) is preferred, the bead body's framing ('rename to drop the _for_test suffix') is incomplete. The real workspace-policy change is documenting MemoryBackend's API stability posture. The current rustdoc says 'API stability is opt-in: it may break across minor versions while the crate is pre-1.0' which is consistent with EITHER path. But path (b) needs an explicit 'these mutation knobs are part of the supported demonstration-backend API surface' statement so consumers know they can rely on the helpers. That documentation work is the actual cost, not the rename.

Not taking action — this is a workspace-architectural choice that crosses canonical-template policy and chat-server's pre-1.0 API surface. The maintainer should pick (a) or (b) explicitly rather than ratify by ambient drift. I would proceed with path (a.1) if asked.
